wv_tilted_tree.blurb: Tilted Tree is a boulder field inside Coopers Rock State Forest in Northern West Virginia, near Morgantown, at roughly 2,000 feet. It is almost entirely bouldering, with a few trad lines and top ropes mixed in. Problems run from V0 up to around V10, but most sit between V0 and V5, so there is plenty for newer boulderers and a handful of hard tests above that. The boulders are bunched into clusters close together, among them Tilted Tree Corridor, Good Block Area, Moby Area and First Wall, which makes it easy to link many problems in one visit. The area is busy on weekends, and holds here can be fragile when damp.

ar_cowell.blurb: Cowell sits in the hills of north-central Arkansas, on the scenic highway through Newton County, at about 2,200 feet. It has a remote, backwoods feel and mixes bouldering, steep sport routes and a smaller amount of trad. Sport climbing is mostly 5.10 to 5.13, with the bulk at 5.11 and 5.12, while the boulder problems run from V0 to the low teens with most between V3 and V9. The largest clusters of climbing are Invasion Area, Font Red, Hudson Mountain and The Hood, with several more small boulder zones scattered around. A great deal of quality rock is packed into a small area.

tx_barton_creek_greenbelt.blurb: The Barton Creek Greenbelt is a strip of park and creek right in Austin, only minutes from downtown, which makes it the nearest outdoor climbing for much of the city. Bouldering and sport routes split most of the climbing, with some top-rope lines and a little trad. Sport routes cluster at 5.10 to 5.12 with a fair number of moderates, and the boulder problems are mostly V0 to V8. Gus Fruh is the biggest wall, a run of overhanging cliffs that form shallow caves, with New Wall, Seismic Wall and Hill of Life nearby. The walk in drops down into cooler shaded air. Summer climbing can be punishing without shade, and cold winter days numb the hands.

ny_crane_mountain.blurb: Crane Mountain is a modest peak in the Adirondack foothills in the town of Johnsburg. Rather than one big cliff, the climbing is spread across several miles of hillside in many separate walls, some as tall as about 320 feet though most routes are a pitch or less. Trad dominates, with a few sport and top-rope lines. Grades run mostly from 5.6 to 5.10, with a handful harder. The rock is solid but often dirty from light traffic, and walk-ins are long and uneven, giving the place an adventurous character. Much recent development has centered on Black Arches Wall and the South Corner Cliffs. Black flies are fierce in May and June.

id_black_cliffs.blurb: The Black Cliffs line Highway 21 a few minutes outside Boise, running toward the Lucky Peak dam, with walls on both sides of the river. The rock is columnar basalt, whose cracks take gear and whose fractures give holds. Trad and sport routes are about evenly split, mostly short, with a few top ropes. Grades center on 5.9 to 5.11, with a solid base of 5.8 and a few climbs at 5.12. Mid Cliffs, Short Cliffs, the Car Body Canyons and Tall Cliffs hold most of the routes. Spring and fall suit it best, since summers get very hot and winters cold. It is a local crag that rarely feels crowded.
